WITH overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(modelconf) as val
  FROM compliancecase
  WHERE modelconf IS NOT NULL
),
status_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    brokrepstat,
    AVG(modelconf) as status_avg
  FROM compliancecase
  WHERE modelconf IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY brokrepstat
),
above_avg_statuses AS (
  SELECT 
    sa.brokrepstat,
    sa.status_avg,
    sa.status_avg - oa.val as above_average
  FROM status_avgs sa
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE oa.val IS NOT NULL
    AND sa.status_avg > oa.val
),
mean_of_qualifying AS (
  SELECT AVG(status_avg) as val
  FROM above_avg_statuses
)
SELECT 
  aas.brokrepstat as status,
  aas.status_avg,
  aas.above_average,
  aas.status_avg / mq.val as ratio
FROM above_avg_statuses aas
CROSS JOIN mean_of_qualifying mq
WHERE mq.val IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY aas.status_avg DESC

assumptions.assumption: NULL brokrepstat values form a single group ('No Status') and are included in the comparison; they are treated as their own distinct status category.
The phrase 'how far above average' means the difference: (status average modelconf) − (overall average modelconf).
The 'mean of the qualifying statuses' averages' refers to the arithmetic mean of the status averages that meet the above-average threshold, computed across all qualifying statuses.
When any reference value (overall average, status average, or mean of qualifying averages) is NULL or undefined, the query returns an empty result set (no rows).
